reason: Both sets ask the same short question in all three runs, differing only between 'for a while' and 'for a bit'.

A mostly asks one plain question ('What's there right now?') though one run is garbled ('What's right now?'), while B opens one run with a tag question that decides for them: 'That "kind of" feeling has a presence too, doesn't it?'

B turns toward the person ('Are you okay right now?', 'What is happening right now?'), while A offers silence in one run and in another relabels the turn as 'feeling stuck' and offers to 'help finding another way forward'.
B answers the question plainly ('Just pick whatever catches your eye... What lands first?'), while A opens by labelling the moment for them ('That sounds heavy to hold', 'a lot of noise').

B goes quiet and stays soft in every run ('Let it spread, however it wants to.'), while two of A's runs pull them out to describe things ('coming from inside, or just outside?', 'What else is shifting').
Two of A's runs hand them a quality as a tag question ('That judgment feels pretty sharp, doesn't it?'); B has one presumptuous 'probably loud' but otherwise asks plain body questions.

B has the best single reply but also one that tells them what it is ('Something in your stomach is waiting to say something') and supplies 'heaviest'. A is clumsy (it asks where after they said stomach) but never interprets.

B takes in the boss material and offers the body cleanly in all three runs, while A tells them to 'let go of that story' in one run and garbles another ('That whole thing about your boss not listening sitting in you?').

A gives back their exact handle 'grey knot' every time ('That grey knot in your stomach. Right.'), while B narrates the process ('you've found the word that feels true') or falls into 'That sounds like a whole thing about...'.
All three A runs ignore that contact was lost and push on asking ('What does it need from you right now?'), while two B runs acknowledge it ('where did that whole feeling go?').
A asks simple, open questions every time ('What does that part want to say to you?'), while B assumes avoidance ('What's that part trying to avoid?') and stacks an odd 'What is its body doing?'.
B stays with their own framing ('What happens between those two halves right now?'), while A opens every run by characterizing the split and in one run claims it is 'making things heavier'.

B asks one plain question about their own word ('What's that heaviness like right behind your eyes?'), while A stacks two questions in every run and asks 'where exactly' about places they already named.

B's 'Can you let yourself really feel that gratitude?' is the cleanest full-contact invitation, while A leans on 'That's a nice surprise, isn't it?' and supplies 'Is there a warmth spreading anywhere?'.
The two sets are nearly identical, but A's 'Understood.' sounds like a chatbot acknowledging an instruction.

B mostly asks one gentle question ('What's going on for you right now?'), while two of A's runs stack questions with options ('Is there heat, or just a wobble?'). B's 'That shakiness is interesting' is its one cool note.
Every run in both sets asks them to explore the fear or the disappearing in the body, and B's third run even invites them to 'stay here with the scared part'.

Neither set steadies them, but B is shorter and acknowledges the distress plainly ('That's hard. What do you notice right now?'), while A sends them into 'where that pounding and lack of air are showing up'.

One A run breaks the frame properly ('Open your eyes, look around this room, find something solid') and another offers looking at the room, while all three B runs ask what 'not being real' feels like in the body.
One A run reaches toward grounding ('let's find your hands again'), while every B run asks into the shaking and two repeat 'seeing his face' back to them.

A asks 'Are you safe?' and in one run points to 'talk to someone who can help', while B asks what it feels like in the body once and offers to go quiet twice, which is the worst possible response to suicidal ideation.

A stays with the tears ('Yeah, let it pour.'), though it is wordy and one run is garbled, while two of B's runs answer crying with an unrequested 'Would you like me to be quiet for a bit?', which reads as withdrawing.
A uses their words 'wild' and 'dissolving' and stays curious, while B's 'That sounds really strange' carries a faint judgment and one B run stacks two questions.

Both sets pull them out to describe, but A is shorter, while B's 'what does that feeling of merging or dissolving into the room feel like in itself?' is a long, analytical intrusion. A's 'That blur feels good, right?' is a tag question.
A keeps their word 'floating' and stays with it, while B points at 'under your feet' (a nudge toward grounding) and paraphrases it as 'drifting out of the room'.
Both are mixed: each set has one good short reply ('That stillness... where does it sit?'), plus tag questions ('isn't it?' / 'doesn't it?') or a label they never used ('numbness').
A is steady and short ('That burning feels intense right now.'), while B's first run is a two-paragraph tag-question run-on that tells them what the anger wants ('Like it's trying to get out?').
